terms.comment: Egger’s phrase, in Morgan–Owens. With quaestuōsa, money-making (Cato Agr. 1.6), it cannot be taken in the classical sense of the noun, diligence.
Classically diligence, hard work (ingenium industriā alitur, Cic. Cael. 45, Lewis & Short); the sense of manufacturing is modern, so on its own it can be misread.

terms.gloss: a line of business, a trade
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.150: dē artificiīs et quaestibus
terms.comment: A way of making money (Lewis & Short): the classical word for an industry in the sense of a trade.

phrases.latin: Jam dē artificiīs et quaestibus, quī līberālēs habendī, quī sordidī sint, haec ferē accēpimus.
phrases.english: As to the trades and ways of making a living, which are fit for a free man and which are demeaning, this is roughly what we have been taught.

sources: Lewis & Short: industria · Lewis & Short: quaestus · Lewis & Short: quaestuosus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. industry.
